item.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
item.description:
U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio unveil a plaque at the Greek foreign ministry in Athens on Oct. 7, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AFP via Getty Images The United States is down one more ambassador. On Oct. 13, 2026, it emerged that President Donald Trump had asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, a MAGA loyalist and ex-fiancée of Trump’s son Donald Jr., to resign her position as U.S. ambassador to Greece , a NATO ally. It follows allegations that the Trump adviser turned diplomat pushed for a Republican donor to pay off her six-figure American Express bill . Guilfoyle later confirmed that she would comply with the request and resigned . In so doing, Athens became one of a number of U.S. overseas missions with a vacancy at the top. item.title: Cornell University bans fraternity parties after alleged gang rape
item.description:
All parties and other social events held in fraternity houses on the campus of Cornell University will be cancelled for the remainder of the 2026-27 school year as the university’s administration contends with a lawsuit alleging a horrific 2024 gang rape in the Chi Phi fraternity house, which has sparked weeks of protest on and off its Ithaca, New York, campus. Michael Kotlikoff, the institution’s president, announced the frat party ban in an email Tuesday afternoon. “These measures will provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life at Cornell to determine whether and how it can safely continue,” Kotlikoff said in his email. item.title: NFL star Tyreek Hill’s estranged wife awarded $500,000 damages in battery trial
item.description:
A jury found former Kansas City and Miami receiver Tyreek Hill liable Tuesday night for two counts of battery in his civil trial. The same Miami jury found him not liable on another five counts of battery, one count of assault, one count of intentional infliction of emotional distress, and one count of continuing domestic violence. The jury awarded Hill's estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro, $500,000 in compensatory damages, but did not award any punitive damages. The trial came about as part of the couple's ongoing divorce in which Vaccaro said Hill physically and verbally abused her during their marriage, including once trying to punch her in the stomach while she was pregnant with their daughter. Hill told jurors that that he did verbally abuse his wife, whom he in turn accused of stealing his money, but the NFL wideout said he did not physically hurt her.

item.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
item.description:
A Ukrainian ex-military officer goes on trial in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source of Russian natural gas. The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert to mount one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. FRANCE 24's Jörg Taszman reports from Berlin, Germany.

Sources: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, France 24

item.title: Turkey: Government raids, takes over top news channel
item.description:
Police raided Turkey's most-watched news channel, Halk TV, early Wednesday, halting broadcasts and installing a government-appointed administrator in the latest move against pro-opposition media. item.title: Ex-NYC Mayor Eric Adams Promised to Pitch a Wisconsin Data Center With ‘Rigor.’ His Failure Was Spectacular.
item.description:
Even for a born pitchman like Eric Adams, a data center was always going to be a tough sell. So when video surfaced of the former New York City mayor being mercilessly heckled by angry residents in a central Wisconsin library as he tried to convince them of the benefits of building a 150-megawatt data center at the site of an old paper mill, the record-scratch, freeze-frame questions asked themselves. How did Adams spend his time in Wisconsin? What was his plan to make this work? And who, exactly, thought this was a good idea? We traveled to Wisconsin Rapids to find out.
